name: Robby the Robot
miniText: How can evolutionary search improve a robot's behavior without directly programming a successful strategy? NetLogo Robby the Robot evolves lookup tables mapping local observations to actions in a can-collecting world. Mitchell's Complexity [1] describes Robby's original teaching example; Holland [2] supplies genetic-search foundations; Mitchell's genetic-algorithm monograph [3] develops selection, recombination, mutation, and evaluation. A strategy is tested through rewards for collecting cans and penalties for inappropriate actions or collisions. Reproduction changes the strategy population, while a separate demonstration shows one controller acting. Performance depends on the reward scheme, evaluation environments, population size, and evolutionary settings. The finite sensor table assumes local observations are sufficient for useful behavior and does not guarantee an optimal policy. Improvement on sampled rooms illustrates adaptation to a specified fitness test, rather than general robotic intelligence or unrestricted real-world transfer.
